The challenge

What makes travel agencies & tour operators different.

01

Custom quotes take hours of copying from old itineraries and rate sheets while travelers shop several agencies.

02

Passport validity, visa appointments, documents and balance payments are chased by phone and spreadsheet.

03

Flight schedule changes and pickup problems surface late, often outside office hours.

04

Repeat travelers are not recognized, so their next trip is booked elsewhere.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for travel agencies & tour operators.

01

AI first-draft itineraries, checked by a consultant

Drafts built only from the agency's past trips, destination notes and contracted rates, with every line sourced and unpriced lines marked for the consultant to complete.

02

Document and visa checklists

Destination templates maintained by consultants from official sources, secure uploads, and reminders before visa, document and supplier name deadlines.

03

Payment milestones

Instalment links through the agency's payment gateway, reconciliation against bookings, and alerts before a late payment puts supplier bookings at risk.

04

Live trip updates

Evening-before itinerary messages, flight change alerts to travelers, drivers and consultants, and one console for the duty consultant.

05

Post-trip feedback and repeat trips

Feedback after return, recovery for problems, review invitations, and consented trip ideas based on past destinations and interests.

Quote, confirm and payAdvanced6–8 weeks

Inquiry-to-itinerary quote with an AI first draft

Turn a traveler's inquiry into a structured brief, assemble a first-draft itinerary from the agency's own past trips and current supplier rates, and let a travel consultant check, price and send it.

Travel agencies & tour operators

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Custom quotes take consultants hours of copying from old itineraries, supplier rate sheets and hotel websites. Travelers shop several agencies at once, so the slowest quote rarely wins. Generic AI trip planners invent hotels, prices and transfer times that the agency would then have to honor or retract.

Trigger

A new inquiry through WhatsApp, the website form, Instagram or email, or a consultant creating a request after a call.

How it runs

  • Capture destination, dates, travelers, budget, hotel category, interests and must-haves into a structured brief, asking follow-up questions on WhatsApp where needed.
  • Retrieve similar past itineraries, approved destination notes and current supplier contracts from the agency's knowledge base.
  • Generate a day-by-day draft that uses only hotels, activities and transfers present in that knowledge base, with the source shown for each line.
  • Pull indicative prices from contracted rate sheets or supplier systems, mark any line without a current rate, and apply the agency's margin rules.
  • Present the draft in an editing view where the consultant adjusts it, confirms availability with suppliers and approves it.
  • Send the branded quote with inclusions, exclusions, cancellation terms and a validity date, and schedule a follow-up.

Human checkpoint

A travel consultant checks every hotel, transfer and price, confirms availability with suppliers and approves the quote before it reaches the traveler. Visa and health guidance in a quote comes only from the consultant, never from the model.

How we measure it

  • Quote-to-booking conversion
  • Draft lines accepted without change
  • Quotes sent with unpriced lines

Prepare for arrivalStandard3–5 weeks

Trip readiness: documents, visas and payment milestones

Give every booked traveler a clear checklist of documents, visa steps and payment dates, send reminders before each cut-off, collect instalments through gateway links, and alert the consultant when anything is late.

Travel agencies & tour operators

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Trips go wrong before departure: passports close to expiry, visa appointments booked late, missing documents for group tours and balance payments chased by phone. Consultants track this in spreadsheets and memory, and supplier deadlines for names and payments are easy to miss.

Trigger

A confirmed booking with departure date, destination and payment schedule, plus supplier deadlines entered by the consultant.

How it runs

  • Build a checklist per traveler from the destination template the agency maintains, covering passport validity, visa type, photos, insurance and supplier name deadlines.
  • Send the checklist through an approved WhatsApp template with a secure upload link, showing each traveler what is done and what is pending.
  • Remind travelers and the consultant at agreed intervals before visa, document and supplier cut-offs, and escalate to the consultant when an item is overdue.
  • Issue a payment link for each instalment through the agency's gateway, reconcile receipts against the booking, and send receipts with tax details prepared by finance.
  • Alert operations when a late payment puts supplier bookings at risk, and pause reminders once the consultant takes over the conversation.

Human checkpoint

Consultants maintain destination checklists from official embassy and visa center sources and confirm visa requirements with each traveler; the automation sends reminders, not advice. Finance owns tax treatment such as TCS on overseas packages, refunds and any change to the payment schedule.

Stay, dine, travel or celebrateStandard4–6 weeks

Live trip updates and on-trip support

Keep travelers informed during the trip with evening-before itinerary messages, pickup details and flight change alerts, and route any problem to the duty consultant with the booking context attached.

Travel agencies & tour operators

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Travelers message their consultant at all hours about pickups, delays and hotel issues, often while the consultant is off shift. Flight schedule changes reach the agency late, drivers and local partners are not updated, and a small problem becomes a lost day.

Trigger

The evening before each itinerary day, a schedule change from the GDS queue or flight status feed, or a traveler message during the trip.

How it runs

  • Send a message the evening before with the next day's timings, pickup point, driver or guide contact and hotel details from the confirmed itinerary.
  • Watch flight segments for schedule changes through the agency's GDS queue or a flight status data provider, and alert the traveler, driver and duty consultant.
  • Classify traveler messages into information requests answered from the confirmed itinerary and problems routed to the duty consultant.
  • Give the duty consultant one view with the booking, supplier contacts and conversation, and log each issue and its resolution.
  • Notify local partners of changed pickup times and confirm the change back to the traveler.

Human checkpoint

The duty consultant handles every problem, rebooking, refund or safety concern; the automation only shares confirmed itinerary information. Emergencies are escalated by phone to the on-call manager.

Feedback and recoveryStandard3–5 weeks

Feedback, service recovery and review replies

Ask every guest for private feedback after a stay, meal, trip or event, open a recovery case when something went wrong, invite every guest to review without filtering, and draft replies to public reviews for a manager to approve.

Hotels & resorts · Restaurants & cloud kitchens · Travel agencies & tour operators · Event & wedding venues

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Unhappy guests often say nothing until they post a review, and happy guests rarely write one unless asked. Replies to Google, OTA and aggregator reviews are slow or generic, and some businesses ask only satisfied guests for reviews, which Google's review policies prohibit.

Trigger

Checkout in the PMS, a closed bill or delivered order, a trip's return date or the day after an event, plus each new public review on a connected platform.

How it runs

  • Send a short private feedback request through an approved template or email, timed for each segment.
  • Open a recovery case for low scores or complaint keywords, assigned to the guest relations, outlet, consultant or event manager with a response target.
  • Send every eligible guest the same review invitation regardless of their feedback score, with no incentive attached.
  • Collect new public reviews from Google Business Profile and other connected sources, and classify sentiment, topics and any serious allegation.
  • Draft a specific, courteous reply in the brand voice from the review and approved facts, and route serious allegations such as food safety, discrimination or injury to the general manager.
  • Post the approved reply through the Google Business Profile API where connected, or give the approver a copy-ready reply for the OTA or aggregator extranet.

Human checkpoint

A named manager edits and approves every public reply and decides every refund, compensation or goodwill gesture. Allegations involving safety, health, discrimination or legal threats go to the general manager or owner before any response.

Return and referStandard4–6 weeks

Repeat guest, loyalty and win-back program

Use visit and booking history to recognize regulars, send consented offers on occasions that matter to each guest, invite lapsed guests back, and remind sales ahead of corporate clients' annual events.

Restaurants & cloud kitchens · Travel agencies & tour operators · Event & wedding venues

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Most hospitality businesses hold years of guest data in POS, booking and CRM systems but rarely use it. Regulars are not recognized, birthdays and anniversaries pass unnoticed, and repeat corporate events go to competitors because nobody called in time. Mass promotions that ignore consent damage trust and break messaging rules.

Trigger

Scheduled segment updates from POS, booking and CRM data, plus date-based triggers such as birthdays, anniversaries, trip anniversaries and the anniversary of a corporate event.

How it runs

  • Build a single guest profile from POS, booking and CRM records with visit frequency, spend band, preferences and consent status per channel.
  • Define segments with the marketing owner, such as regulars, lapsed guests, occasion dates, repeat travelers by destination interest and corporate event clients.
  • Send approved marketing templates or emails only to guests with marketing opt-in, with an opt-out in every message and frequency caps.
  • Track visit-based rewards in the POS loyalty module for restaurants, suggest trips from past destinations for travel, and alert venue sales managers ahead of a client's annual event date.
  • Measure returns, bookings and opt-outs per campaign against a holdout group, and retire offers that do not bring guests back.

Human checkpoint

The marketing owner approves segments, offers and every template. The sales manager decides and makes outreach to corporate and event clients personally. Discounts beyond agreed limits need owner approval.

Profiles of inactive guests are deleted after an agreed period.

How we measure it

  • Opt-out rate per campaign
